issues.description: Constructor signature and attributes for class 'Animal' differ between the problem statement/template and the solution. The problem statement UML and the example in the template Main() imply Animal and its concrete subclasses should have a single-argument constructor that initializes only the 'name' (examples: Seal("Clarabelle"), Pig("Doodle"), Goat("Buttinsky")). The solution's Animal class declares an additional field 'age' (private int age) and defines a constructor Animal(String name, int age); its concrete subclasses (Seal, Pig, Goat) also define two-parameter constructors (String name, int age). This mismatch (extra constructor parameter and attribute in the solution) conflicts with the UML and the template examples and will confuse students about which constructor signature and attributes they must implement and use.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor/attribute expectations consistent across artifacts. Options: (A) Modify the solution to provide single-argument constructors that match the UML/template (e.g., add Animal(String name) and corresponding single-arg constructors in Seal/Pig/Goat that delegate to a two-arg constructor or omit 'age'), and remove or make 'age' optional; or (B) Update the problem statement UML and the template Main() examples to include the 'age' attribute and require two-argument constructors (String name, int age). If you want to preserve solution details while keeping template examples valid, add convenience single-arg constructors in the solution that delegate to the two-arg constructor with a sensible default age.
